findings.summary: Absence of a detected Git worktree is incorrectly treated as proof that a file mutation is DIRECT.
findings.detail: FILE_MUTATION is project-natured only when gitToplevel() succeeds. Calling evaluate({operation: FILE_MUTATION, targetPath: '/work/new-project/src/app.ts'}) before git initialization—or omitting targetPath entirely—sets projectNatured=false and returns an allowed DIRECT decision without a run. This bypasses CP-HI-01 and the Repo Factory requirement that actual repository creation enter a managed PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP run. The code also fails to consult registered checkout paths before allowing the write.
findings.suggestedFix: Reject FILE_MUTATION without a target. Distinguish trusted independent-artifact creation from project/bootstrap mutation explicitly, and consult registered managed checkout/bootstrap scope instead of using Git detection as the sole classifier.

findings.summary: Git probe failures silently degrade to “not a repository” and can produce an allowed DIRECT write.
findings.detail: The catch converts every execFileSync or realpathSync failure—including missing Git, permission errors, dubious-ownership rejection, and filesystem failures—to null. ManagedWriteGuard then treats a FILE_MUTATION as non-project-natured and allows it. Sequence: target a real repository, force rev-parse to fail, receive null, then obtain DIRECT_WRITE allowance. This directly violates CP-HI-08's prohibition on treating probe failure as PASS.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a discriminated probe result for INSIDE, OUTSIDE, and ERROR. Fail closed on ERROR and only classify OUTSIDE when non-membership was established reliably.

findings.summary: Relative paths are resolved against the daemon process cwd rather than the tool operation's cwd.
findings.detail: GuardRequest explicitly accepts relative targets, but canonical() uses resolve(path) with process.cwd() and receives no execution base directory. Sequence: the daemon cwd is /service, a tool executes in /work/repo, and targetPath='src/app.ts'; the guard inspects /service/src/app.ts and may allow DIRECT while the tool mutates /work/repo/src/app.ts. CP-HI-01 therefore does not guard the path actually written.
findings.suggestedFix: Require absolute target paths, or include a trusted execution cwd and resolve both authorization and execution against that exact canonical directory.

findings.summary: Authorization is role-blind and permits a bound blind-review session to mutate the reviewed candidate.
findings.detail: The assignments query selects no role and accepts every active assignment attached to the run or one of its tasks. A BLIND_REVIEWER assignment has run_id set, so its session and generation pass authorizeSession; a subsequent FILE_MUTATION inside a participating checkout returns WRITE_ALLOWED. That makes the blind reviewer a producer, violating CP-HI-04.
findings.suggestedFix: Select and validate assignment.role. Explicitly reject BLIND_REVIEWER for all candidate mutations and use operation-specific role allowlists for privileged writes.

findings.summary: Same-worktree and same-branch claims can be bypassed because the guard checks only exact-path claims.
findings.detail: authorizeTarget queries only resource_claims.declared_path. Sequence: Run A holds a worktree or branch claim; Run B skips claim acquisition and evaluates a FILE_MUTATION or GIT_COMMIT in that same worktree. If the exact path is not separately claimed, Run B is allowed. This bypasses the §23.2 hard rejects and CP-S13; the guard does not require Run B to hold any current claim either.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve and validate the operation's worktree and branch claims at authorization time, reject claims held by other runs, and require the requesting run's applicable claim to be current, unexpired, and owned by a current generation.

findings.summary: Supplying targetPath disables validation of the requested remote repository identity.
findings.detail: repositoryIdentity participation is checked only when an ALWAYS_MANAGED operation has no resolvedPath. A caller with a valid run for repository A can request GITHUB_PR, GITHUB_RULESET, or PROGRAMMATIC_MERGE for unrelated repository B while supplying a path inside A's checkout; the filesystem branch ignores B and returns allowed. The declared operation target is therefore outside the run's authority.
findings.suggestedFix: Use operation-specific target validation. GitHub operations must always validate their actual remote identity; if local context is also supplied, require it to resolve to that same registered repository.

findings.summary: A nested or submodule repository is authorized as its containing participant repository.
findings.detail: The actual worktree discovered at line 131 is never matched to a participant. Instead, any participant checkout containing resolvedPath becomes owner. Sequence: Run A includes outer repository /work/A, while /work/A/vendor/B is a separate Git repository not in the run; a mutation under B has worktree=/work/A/vendor/B but owner resolves to A and is allowed. Claims are also queried under A's identity, bypassing claims held for B.
findings.suggestedFix: Bind authorization to the canonical gitToplevel result and the corresponding registered repository checkout. Reject nested unregistered worktrees and choose the exact/deepest participant deterministically.

findings.summary: Authorization is a detached, unfenced check that can become stale before the write occurs.
findings.detail: evaluate() reads run, binding, and claim state and returns a plain GuardGrant; the grant contains neither operation, binding generation, claim identity/version, expiry, nor a single-use fence. Sequence: evaluate succeeds for generation 1, generation 1 is revoked or the run becomes non-ACTIVE, then the caller performs the write using the prior grant. The write occurs without a valid managed identity, violating CP-HI-01. Claim acquisition can race in the same window.
findings.suggestedFix: Perform authorization and dispatch inside the trusted adapter at act time. Bind any unavoidable grant to the exact operation, target, binding generation, and current claim lease, make it single-use/short-lived, and revalidate immediately before the side effect.

findings.summary: Canonicalization drops the first character of a missing top-level path component.
findings.detail: When parent is the filesystem root, parent already ends with the separator, but slice(parent.length + 1) skips one extra character. For example, canonical('/definitely-new/file') returns '/efinitely-new/file' when only '/' exists. The guard can consequently authorize and record a path different from the one the caller will write.
findings.suggestedFix: Use basename(cursor), or account for roots that already end in a separator when extracting the missing component.
